title: Self-coach notebook: manager prep and quarterly goals
content:
Purpose: quick, searchable scratchpad for weekly manager prep, quarterly goals, and ad-hoc performance anecdotes. Not polished — mostly prompts, datapoints, and rehearsal lines for 1:1s and quarterly check-ins.

---
Top-level goals (Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026)
- Reduce time-to-fulfill employee access requests from average 3.2 days -> target 1.5 days (metric tracked in HR-TICKET-2045).
- Build and launch onboarding mini-playbook for Dedicated/Private sales hires (owner: me; deadline: 2026-01-30).
- Run two manager enablement workshops focused on asynchronous feedback and calibration (target: >70% manager attendance).
- Pilot micro-coaching program with engineering managers (5 managers, 8-week pilot). Measure: manager confidence + direct report NPS.

Accomplishments to highlight (last 6 months)
- Launched shared template for ramp plans adapted for Dedicated team — reduced ramp confusion in 3 hires (Jira PR #342).
- Negotiated new external vendor rate that saved ~$18k/year for candidate assessment tool (procurement email thread link above).
- Ran cross-functional calibration session that resolved 6 leveling inconsistencies across infra/platform teams (notes in confluence link).

Manager prep: things I want to discuss
- Headcount ask: +1 full-time for onboarding ops to support Dedicated onboarding spikes. Rationale: current bandwidth leads to 40% increase in time-to-activate in peak weeks.
- Compensation calibration: present comparable benchmarks for Senior TPM vs Senior PM on infra. Bring sample comp data and 2 case examples.
- Risks: growing backlog of EoL training updates (security/compliance). Need prioritization and 2 sprints of support.
- Development ask: request mentorship pairing with Senior People Partner (ops org). Goal: improve coaching cadence and stakeholder negotiation skills.

Self-eval bullets (to use in self-review)
- Strength: cross-team influence — consistently brought engineering, product, and SRE stakeholders to alignment on hiring profiles and ramp expectations.
- Area to improve: delegation — I still own too much of the onboarding checklist; aim to codify automation and hand-off in the next quarter.
- Metric-based claim: reduced mean time-to-answer for new-hire questions in slack by ~28% after creating FAQ channel and weekly office hours.

Anecdotes / Evidence to surface (short snippets)
- "Onboarding - Dedicated: Candidate A had faster access provisioning because we used the new checklist; they completed first-week training 2 days earlier than previous hires." (link to onboarding sheet row ID: HR-ONB-078)
- "Calibration: Manager X changed hire banding after our session; provided written note acknowledging the calibration outcome." (attach before/after notes in PRs).

Manager coaching prompts (to practice aloud)
- "If I could use your support, it would be by helping unblock headcount approval for onboarding ops; I have a cost/benefit + risk slide ready. Can we align on owner and timeline?"
- "When you think about my growth, where should I prioritize: stakeholder influence vs. deep program execution? Examples are helpful."

Meeting action items (post-1:1)
- Share slide deck for headcount ask + 1-pager by EOD Tuesday.
- Schedule preliminary interview with Senior People Partner for mentorship (target start: Apr 2026).
- Follow up on procurement vendor contract renewal and confirm savings figure; loop in finance.

Quick checklist (weekly)
- [ ] Update ramp-playbook doc with any changes from last hire
- [ ] Review outstanding access tickets (filter: people-ops, priority: P1)
- [ ] Drop 3 short notes to managers in pilot cohort (status, ask, resource)
- [ ] Prep 3 talking points for tomorrow's 1:1 (use top 3 bullets above)

Notes to self (rough / half-formed)
- Consider running a "office hours" 25-min slot twice a week instead of 1hr once — test adoption.
- Experiment: create a short microsurvey (3 Qs) after onboarding week 1 to capture early friction points.
- Could build a simple dashboard for onboarding KPIs using existing internal BI workspace; ask BI partner for a 2-hr scope call.

Open questions / unknowns
- What is the funding timeline for Dedicated expansion hires? (Finance planning doc?)
- Which senior leader owns the security EoL training priority? Need to surface at exec-ops if not resolved by next week.

Next actions (this week)
- Draft headcount one-pager and run it by Jordan.
- Pull ticket metrics for access requests (last 6 months) and create a small chart to show average/median.
- Add onboarding pulse survey to HR pipeline for pilot hires.

Scratch ideas (low-effort experiments)
- "Quick wins" card in onboarding: 3 things every new hire should do in week 1 (Slack channel, payroll check, health/benefits).
- Monthly "manager micro-lesson" email: 1-minute read with a single tactic (asynchronous feedback, hire interview question bank).

Attachments / refs to find later
- onboarding-playbook-v3 (confluence)
- Jira filter: project = HR AND label = access-request AND created >= -180d
- PR: github.com/redwood/ops-onboarding/pull/342

End note: keep this doc lean — copy snippets into formal self-review when close to submission. Use this as rehearsal notes when practicing aloud before manager meetings.

-----
Revision log (quick)
- 2025-10-15: initial draft
- 2026-01-12: added pilot plan for micro-coaching
- 2026-03-05: updated metrics and headcount ask language prior to manager sync
